title: Car won't start clicking noise

causes.text: Starter turns slowly/dim lights: battery discharged or terminals loose/corroded
causes.document: 2022 Toyota Camry Owner's Manual OM06244U (year mapping per Helm listing; manual is Camry-specific)
causes.appliesTo: Toyota Camry; manual does not use the word 'clicking'

causes.text: Starter does not turn over: battery discharged, terminal disconnected, steering lock malfunction
causes.document: 2022 Toyota Camry Owner's Manual OM06244U (year mapping per Helm listing; manual is Camry-specific)

guidancePrimary: universal: Car Care Council — dead batteries are a leading cause of starting failure; dim headlights or interior lights, accessories that fail to operate, or an illuminated battery light are the signs to check the battery

guidance.document: Car Care Council, "Summer Heat Takes a Toll on Your Car's Battery" (published 2020-07-21; non-profit consumer education organization)
guidance.text: Dead batteries are a leading cause of starting failure. Check the battery if you notice headlights and interior lights dim, accessories that fail to operate, or the battery light illuminated. Frequent engine on/off cycles also wear the starter.
guidance.answers: can_i_keep_driving: the engine will not run, so the car cannot be driven; the Car Care Council identifies dead batteries as a leading cause of starting failure and lists dim lights, failing accessories and an illuminated battery light as the signs to check the battery

guidance.text: The starter motor turns over slowly, the interior lights and headlights are dim, or the horn does not sound or sounds at a low volume. ... The battery may be discharged.
guidance.quote: The starter motor turns over slowly, the interior lights and headlights are dim, or the horn does not sound or sounds at a low volume. ... The battery may be discharged.
guidance.answers: check yourself first: battery (jump start p.562); manual never uses the word 'clicking' — mapping clicking→this row is our inference, so wording on page must not claim the manual says 'clicking'

firstStep.document: Car Care Council, "Summer Heat Takes a Toll on Your Car's Battery" (published 2020-07-21; non-profit consumer education organization)
firstStep.text: Check the battery first: the Car Care Council lists dim headlights or interior lights, accessories that fail to operate, and an illuminated battery light as the signs that the battery should be checked. The vehicle's own manual documents jump starting as the test for a discharged battery — see the vehicle-specific entries below.
firstStep.answers: check yourself first: the warning signs are observable without tools; a discharged battery is confirmed by a jump start per the vehicle manual

hub.note: Rapid clicking with dimming lights points at the battery, its terminals or the ground strap rather than the starter: there is enough current to pull the solenoid in, not enough to turn the engine. A single heavy clunk is the opposite case — current reaches the starter and it does not spin.
hub.verdict: Not a safety issue — the car is stationary until it starts.
